subject: Seed-era budget alignment & committed-use proposal — next steps
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.inference>
To: Ella Ramirez <ella@clearmap.ai>, Procurement Team <procurement@clearmap.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-10-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick recap + ask: token volumes & budget bands from today’s call

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Short recap and two asks so we can build a tailored committed-use proposal:

Recap (high level):
- Clearmap is prototyping a user-facing summarization feature for field teams (short-form generation + 512-token summaries).
- Expected ramp: pilot (Q1) ~ 200M tokens/mo, production (Q3) 1.5–2.0B tokens/mo, long-term >5B tokens/mo for multi-product rollout.
- Primary constraints: predictable unit cost and auditability (retention 30 days), legal wants a simple committed SKU.

Asks: 
1) Can you confirm a short-term budget range for proof-of-concept (monthly $ budget) — ballpark is fine.
2) Do you have a target $/1M tokens that would make a committed deal compelling for Clearmap?

I attached our Startup Tiers PDF and a lightweight commitment worksheet to make it easier to model (RDL-Startup-Tiers.pdf, Commitment-worksheet-Clearmap.xlsx). If you prefer, we can sketch three scenarios (starter, scale, enterprise) and a 1/2/3-year commit path.

Next step: once you share the budget band and target $/1M tokens, I’ll run this with Ben + RevOps and return a recommended structure (startup credit + committed discount tiers + multi-year incentive).

Thanks — Soojin
Soojin Lee | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.inference | +1 (415) 555-0192

---
Attachment: RDL-Startup-Tiers.pdf (1 page summary of starter credits and eligibility)
Attachment: Commitment-worksheet-Clearmap.xlsx (simple model: months, tokens/mo, $/1M, discount)
From: Ella Ramirez <ella@clearmap.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.inference>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@clearmap.ai>
Date: 2026-10-28T11:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + ask: token volumes & budget bands from today’s call

Thanks, Soojin — and appreciate the workbook. Quick answers below: 

1) Budget band for POC (monthly): $8k–$12k (we can stretch to $18k if unit economics are favorable).
2) Target unit: ideally <= $650 per 1M tokens for the POC to get buy-in from product/finance. For production scale (1.5–2B/mo) we’d need to see something in the $300–$400 per 1M range to be sustainable.

Notes: we can do a 12–24 month committed contract if the discounts justify an initial financial commitment; procurement will need simple terms and an annual review clause.

Happy to hop back on a quick call if helpful.

— Ella
VP Product, Clearmap
ella@clearmap.ai
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.inference>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-10-28T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Clearmap answers on budget/target (seed-era) — need pricing guidance

Ben / Marissa — forwarding Ella’s note. Key points: POC budget $8k–$12k/mo (stretch to $18k) and they want <= $650/1M tokens for POC; production target $300–$400/1M at 1.5–2B/mo.

Can we map 1) a starter offer that combines startup credits and a priced committed SKU for POC, and 2) a multi-year committed path for scale? Also confirm whether we can flex the startup program for a faster ramp (one-off extra credit) and whether legal can accept a 12-month auto-renew with annual review.

I attached the commitment worksheet they’ll use to plug numbers.

Thanks — Soojin
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-10-29T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Clearmap answers on budget/target (seed-era) — need pricing guidance

Good notes. Quick thoughts:
- Startup program: we can offer the standard 3-month starter bundle (50% credits up to $12k) + one-time 10% extra credit for high-probability logos — call that "starter boost".
- Committed-use: propose tiered discounts by monthly token commit: 0.2–0.5B/mo = 15% off list; 0.5–1.5B/mo = 25% off; >1.5B/mo = 35% off. With sample math that would get them into the $300–$400/1M range at higher commits depending on model choice and quantization.
- Multi-year incentive: add a 5% one-time rebate payable after year 1 for a 2-year commit, or 10% for a 3-year if they prepay 9 months.

Constraints: need RevOps sanity check on how we map list $/1M to discounted outcomes (model family matters). Also legal prefers 12-month initial terms with optional auto-renew, avoid complicated early-termination credits.

Ask Marissa: if this structure looks good, can you draft a short template SOW/commitment sheet and confirm what legal wants for the wording on rebates?

— Ben
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-10-29T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Clearmap answers on budget/target (seed-era) — need pricing guidance

Thanks — I’ll draft a 1-page commitment summary (starter + committed tiers + multi-year incentive table) and a short legal appendix. High-level edits:
- Rename "rebate" to "performance credit" for clarity; payout options: invoice credit versus one-time prepayment reduction.
- For the starter boost, limit to customers with signed MSA within 30 days of POC start.
- On pricing math: I’ll attach worksheets with two model variants (base LLM and quantized variant) so we can show $/1M outputs.

I’ll circulate a draft by Friday EOD.

— Marissa
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.inference>
To: Ella Ramirez <ella@clearmap.ai>, Procurement Team <procurement@clearmap.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-11-02T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: POC starter + committed path (clearmap) — attached summary & next steps

Ella — thanks for the patience. Attached is a short proposal reflecting the internal guidance: RDL-Startup-Tiers.pdf (attached earlier) plus a 1-page commitment summary and the completed Commitment-worksheet-Clearmap.xlsx. Highlights:

POC (months 0–3)
- Starter boost: 50% credits up to $12k across 3 months, + 10% one-time extra credit if MSA signed within 30 days. Effective POC spend: up to $18k creditable.
- If they accept the committed SKU during POC (min 200M tokens/mo), we’ll price at an effective $600/1M tokens for the duration of month 1–3 (after credits applied).

Production target (1.5–2B/mo) — proposed committed tiers:
- 0.2–0.5B/mo: 15% discount (ballpark $480–$510/1M)
- 0.5–1.5B/mo: 25% discount (ballpark $360–$420/1M)
- >1.5B/mo: 35% discount (ballpark $260–$340/1M)

Multi-year incentive:
- 2-year commit: +5% performance credit at end of year 1
- 3-year commit: +10% performance credit if prepay >= 9 months

Next steps:
1) Confirm whether Clearmap wants the starter boost and whether procurement is OK with a 12-month subscription term with annual review.
2) If yes, I’ll send a DocuSign for MSA + Appendix A (commitment sheet) with the numbers pre-filled.

DocuSign (preview): https://www.docusign.com/link/preview/RDL-Clearmap-349
Drive link to worksheet: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2b3Cstartuptiers

If you want a quick math call I’m free today 3–4pm PT.

Best — Soojin
From: Procurement Team <procurement@clearmap.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.inference>
Cc: Ella Ramirez <ella@clearmap.ai>
Date: 2026-11-02T17:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: POC starter + committed path (clearmap) — next steps

Thanks, Soojin — procurement has reviewed the commitment summary. Quick answers:
- Starter boost: approved, provided the MSA is standard and the extra credit is applied as an invoice credit.
- Term: procurement is comfortable with 12-month initial term with annual review.
- DocuSign preview looks fine — please send the final MSA + Appendix A.
- We will aim to sign within 10 business days of receiving final documents.

We appreciate the clear pricing bands. Please also include a short clause on data retention and audit logs (30-day retention as discussed).

— Procurement Team, Clearmap
